target_customer: Women buying and selling pre-owned designer apparel and accessories who worry about counterfeits
problem: Online auction sites were full of counterfeit luxury goods, so buyers could not trust listings and honest sellers were drowned out.
business_model: marketplace take rate on auctions of pre-screened items, plus a paid authentication service

founders.name: Fei Deyle
founders.background_notes: Per TechCrunch (2013-03-17) the idea came from her fashion blog, where she wrote guides on spotting counterfeits and consignment stores asked her to authenticate items.

founders.name: Travis Deyle
founders.background_notes: Named as a co-founder in the TechCrunch launch article; not listed on the YC page.

founders.name: David Mohs
founders.background_notes: Named in the TechCrunch launch article.

exit.reason: The company states the peer to peer marketplace closed in 2020 because payment processors such as PayPal changed their fee structures; the authentication service continues.

competitors.name: eBay
competitors.what: General online auction marketplace with a known counterfeit problem for luxury goods

competitors.name: Tradesy
competitors.what: Peer to peer resale marketplace that relaunched as a luxury fashion platform in October 2012

technical_complexity.rationale: A standard auction marketplace; the hard part was human authentication expertise, not software.

defensibility.rationale: The authentication know how of the founder was a trust asset, but any marketplace or consignment player could hire authenticators.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The marketplace persisted about a decade and closed in 2020 after payment processor changes, per the company; larger resale players such as The RealReal grew in the same period (not sourced here).

market_need_then: Counterfeit luxury goods were a recognized problem on eBay in 2013, and the founder's blog audience and consignment stores asked for authentication help, per TechCrunch.

branding.domain_note: Exact lollipuff.com, in use since at least the 2013 launch.

identity.logo: Wordmark; no source describes it in detail

branding.brand_signature: The authenticity guarantee and certificate lookup
branding.community_and_virality: Founder was a known online authenticator and the site shows press logos such as TechCrunch, Forbes and Marie Claire.

brand_strength.rationale: Known in the authentication niche and cited by press, but no sign of mass brand pull.

pivots.from: peer to peer authenticated auction marketplace
pivots.why: Marketplace closed as payment processors changed fee structures, per the company.

outcome_analysis: Lollipuff built trust in luxury resale through founder led authentication and ran a marketplace for about ten years. It raised little visible venture money, and the company says the marketplace closed in 2020 when payment processors changed fee structures, which points to platform dependency, while the authentication business survives as a niche service. The YC directory still lists it as Active.
notes: Funding: an aggregator snippet gave $125k (Dealroom) and $20K (CB Insights, YC as investor); these conflict and are unverified, so no round is recorded. The 2020 marketplace closure is stated on the company's own about page. Exit type unknown because the company continues as an authentication service. The Tradesy entry is from a Wikipedia mirror seen only in a search snippet. Searches for the name origin found nothing.
